lines.text: Every great fast bowler spends years learning one thing.
This one learned it in six hours.
And nobody taught it a thing.
At the start, it's hopeless.
Random speeds, random lengths. It gets hit on more than half its balls.
Its opponents are three batters, each with a hidden weakness.
The Slogger. He hits anything full or short. But a yorker on the stumps, or a slower ball, can get him.
The Technician. He leaves anything wide and blocks the straight ball. His only flaw: a good length ball that moves away late.
And the Tailender. Brave, but not much of a batter.
And all three learn. Bowl the same ball twice, and they're ready for it.
The bowler is a tiny brain. Eighteen numbers in, about the batter and the over. Four out: speed, length, line and swing.
A hundred and ninety two brains bowl. The best survive, and breed the next generation.
Fifteen hundred generations. About eighty three million deliveries.
And then, it got good. Suspiciously good.
It had found a trick. Bouncer. Yorker. Bouncer. Yorker.
Flat out, then dead slow. Three bouncers an over, which is illegal.
It hadn't learned to bowl. It had learned to fool my batters.
So I made the batters smarter. Now they spot patterns.
Alternate bouncer and yorker, and they've read you by the fourth ball.
And only two bouncers an over, like the real laws.
Then I deleted everything, and started again.
Fifteen hundred generations later, every ball lands where it means to.
Against the Technician, it bowls good length on fourth stump, seventy three percent of the time, and gives away barely one run an over.
Then, the one that moves away.
Edged. Gone.
The Slogger fights back. Four. Four. Four. His confidence is climbing.
But the bowler keeps it full and straight, until one yorker is too good.
And the Tailender? It skips the bouncer and goes full and straight. Trapped in front.
You can watch it decide. Every neuron, every ball.
Scored against the hand written expert plan for each batter, the final brain beats every one.
And the cheating version, retested under the new rules? Not even close.
No coaching. No examples. Just a reward, a few hard lessons, and evolution.
This is the machine that learned to bowl.
